experiment_description: Central concept and measurement configuration: use proton-proton collisions recorded with the CMS detector at the CERN LHC at center-of-mass energy sqrt(s)=13 TeV to treat the spin-1/2 top quark and top antiquark in top-quark-pair production as a two-qubit quantum system. The analysis uses the published CMS doubly differential lepton+jets measurement of top-quark and antiquark polarization coefficients and spin-correlation coefficients in bins of the top-pair invariant mass m(ttbar) and the absolute top production angle |cos(theta)|, where theta is defined in the ttbar center-of-mass frame with respect to the proton-beam direction. The lepton+jets topology consists of one W boson decaying leptonically and the other hadronically; the spin analyzers are the charged lepton and the down-type quark from the W decay. The spatial-geometric analogue for this collider measurement is the resolved two-dimensional phase-space scope: m(ttbar) bins [300,400], [400,600], [600,800], and [800,13000] GeV crossed with |cos(theta)| bins [0.0,0.4], [0.4,0.7], and [0.7,1.0]. The spin basis is the helicity basis, an event-dependent right-handed coordinate system in the ttbar rest frame with unit vectors (khat, nhat, rhat), where khat is the top-quark flight direction, rhat=(phat-cos(theta) khat)/sin(theta), nhat=rhat x khat, phat is the proton-beam direction, and the sign convention is nhat -> sgn(cos(theta)) nhat, rhat -> sgn(cos(theta)) rhat, khat -> khat. Because this basis changes orientation with event kinematics, the derived spin states correspond to the event-dependent, or fictitious, quantum-state construction used to characterize the hierarchy of quantum correlations. In each phase-space bin reconstruct the two-qubit spin density matrix rho_ttbar = (1/4)[I2 tensor I2 + sum_i P_i sigma_i tensor I2 + sum_j Pbar_j I2 tensor sigma_j + sum_ij C_ij sigma_i tensor sigma_j], where I2 is the 2 by 2 identity, sigma_i are Pauli matrices, P_i and Pbar_j are the top and antitop polarization components, and C_ij is the 3 by 3 spin-correlation matrix. Evaluate: top-quark discord D_t = S(rho_antitop) - S(rho_ttbar) + min_uhat[p_+ S(rho_top,+uhat)+p_- S(rho_top,-uhat)], where S(rho)=-Tr(rho log2 rho), uhat is the projective spin-measurement axis on the antitop, p_+ and p_- are the corresponding outcome probabilities, and rho_top,+uhat and rho_top,-uhat are the post-measurement top-quark states; the entanglement marker Delta_E from the Peres-Horodecki criterion as reported for the same reconstructed density matrices, with Delta_E greater than 1 defining the entangled region; the steering marker T = integral d^2 uhat sqrt(uhat^T C^T C uhat), with the integration over all unit-vector orientations and threshold 2*pi; the Bell-correlation marker B=m1+m2, where m1 and m2 are the two largest eigenvalues of C^T C and threshold is 1 for CHSH Bell-correlated states; and the mixed-state quantum magic M2_tilde = -log2([1+sum_i(P_i^4+Pbar_i^4)+sum_ij C_ij^4]/[1+sum_i(P_i^2+Pbar_i^2)+sum_ij C_ij^2]). For each observable, use the Gaussian likelihood -2 log L = sum_ij (o_i-x_i) U_ij^{-1} (o_j-x_j), where o_i are the measured polarization and spin-correlation coefficients in the specified bin, U_ij is their covariance matrix, and x_i are the fitted coefficients constrained to the physical interval [-1,1]; central observable values are obtained at the likelihood minimum while holding the relevant observable definition fixed.
